A one-particle hitting probability is at least Φ(−ℓ/√q) by terminal law. For t≤γ^(−1), E sup_{s≤t}X(s)≤sqrt[14/(3π)]/(1−e^(−1))√q<2√q using integrated velocity first moments; Borell yields upper bound exp[−(ℓ/√q−2)_+²/2]. Independence then forces T_N/t_N→P1 uniformly in arbitrary nonnegative triangular arrays by choosing (1±ε)t_N and Gaussian Mills estimates. The two scaling regimes arise by asymptotically inverting the exact q threshold, not numerical extrapolation. Independent variance/root checks corroborate finite instances.
